maria.dev: Hey folks, running into duplicate POSTs from the onboarding sample on Android 12 emulator. Sequence: app cold start -> network flaps -> two token refreshes happen concurrently -> both original uploads replay = duplicate records. Anyone seen a refresh stampede like this?

alexg: That pattern rings a bell. Are you doing refresh in an Interceptor? Interceptor + suspend functions often race since interceptors run on OkHttp worker threads.

maria.dev: Yea using an Interceptor. Pseudocode: ```override fun intercept(chain): Response { if (tokenExpired()) { token = refreshToken() } return chain.proceed(chain.request().newBuilder().header("Authorization","Bearer $token").build()) }``` refreshToken is suspend and calls our auth service. We tried synchronized(lock) around refresh but still saw two refreshes.

sam: Interceptors are executed per-call on dispatcher threads. synchronized(lock) can fail if refresh happens on different thread pools or if coroutine dispatchers change. OkHttp's Authenticator is designed for 401 flows and will serialize retries for the same call.

jordan: Also check WorkManager/Retry interplay. If a background worker is retried while one instance is already refreshing, you'll get duplicate refresh flows. We fixed by centralizing token state in a singleton that exposes a refresh Deferred and using Mutex.withLock or a single-flight promise so only one refresh happens at a time.

alexg: Another pragmatic layer: add idempotency keys to uploads on the server side so duplicate POSTs are harmless. Also make sure refreshToken surfaces failure types properly so worker backoff doesn't blindly re-enqueue immediate retries.

maria.dev: Does the android-sdk provide a helper for single-flight refresh? I couldn't find one; sample app uses an Interceptor which might be encouraging the anti-pattern.

sam: Not currently in stable releases. There's an internal snippet we use in platform teams: a TokenProvider with an atomic reference to a Deferred<Token> and compare-and-set to publish the active refresh. Or simpler: a Mutex and store lastSuccessfulToken/time to short-circuit.

jordan: Example pattern: ```suspend fun getToken(): String { mutex.withLock { if (!expired(cached)) return cached.token if (ongoingRefresh != null) return ongoingRefresh.await() ongoingRefresh = async { doRefresh() } try { val t = ongoingRefresh.await(); cached = t; return t } finally { ongoingRefresh = null } } }``` That avoids double refresh across coroutines/workers.

alexg: If you switch to Authenticator, beware: Authenticator receives a Route/Response and runs synchronously on the OkHttp thread. Use blocking refresh there or adapt with runBlocking carefully. Mixing runBlocking and suspend can deadlock if you're on the same dispatcher used by your HTTP calls.

maria.dev: Good call. So recommended plan: 1) move 401 handling to an Authenticator or central TokenProvider; 2) protect refresh with Mutex/single-flight; 3) add idempotency keys to uploads; 4) ensure WorkManager backoff isn't immediate.

ci-bot: PR #3421 opened by @alexg: adds devex/samples/token-refresh-singleflight.kt and a short note in docs/devex/auth.md :eyes:

maria.dev: Thanks, will try those changes and report back with logs if it still repros. Appreciate the quick help :thumbsup:
